artworks.title: The Death of Hyacinthos
artworks.description: Broc's Apollo and the dying Hyacinth — Amyclas' most famous son, the Laconian prince whose death makes the flower and whose father founded Amyclae.

artworks.title: Apollo and Hyacinth
artworks.description: Domenichino's Farnese fresco: Apollo with Hyacinth — Amyclas' line as the Spartan house behind the god's beloved youth.

artworks.title: The Death of Hyacinth
artworks.description: Tiepolo's Thyssen canvas: Hyacinth fallen — the Amyclid prince as Venetian colour, Amyclas' dynasty remembered through the son's death.

popCulture.title: Amyclas of Sparta
popCulture.description: King of Laconia, son of Lacedaemon — eponym of Amyclae and father of Hyacinthus. Not every minor Amyclas of the catalogues.

popCulture.title: Hyacinth
popCulture.description: Amyclas' son beloved of Apollo — the youth whose blood becomes the hyacinth flower.

popCulture.title: Amyclae
popCulture.description: The Laconian town named for Amyclas — seat of the throne and of Apollo Hyacinthius' cult.

popCulture.title: Lacedaemon (mythology)
popCulture.description: Amyclas' father — the eponym who gives Laconia its other name before the Amyclid kings.
